question: Does a replication from the public data reproduce Card and Krueger's (1994) difference-in-differences estimate of the change in full-time-equivalent employment per store in New Jersey relative to eastern Pennsylvania, and does the estimate survive a robustness check fixed in advance from the later literature?
hypotheses: H1: The replicated headline difference-in-differences estimate matches the published estimate to the precision the published table reports.
H2: The pre-specified robustness check yields an estimate of the same sign as the headline estimate.
contribution: An independent, fully logged replication of a canonical difference-in-differences estimate from the authors' public data, with one robustness check chosen before any estimate is computed.

tasks.title: The published estimates and definitions; later critiques and robustness checks (e.g. Neumark-Wascher payroll data, Card-Krueger 2000 reply)
